column1: # Where each woven Spanish plural in lex-es.tsv was read.
# A noun row weaves its second form under an English plural, and the tooltip
# prints that form as the word the reader met. On 2026-10-08 every woven
# Spanish plural was read in the headword line of English Wiktionary's
# Spanish entry for its noun, rendered as a reader sees it, because the raw
# template mostly leaves the plural to Wiktionary's module: {{es-noun|m}}
# prints "hombre m (plural hombres)". 177 of the 178 are among the plurals
# their own noun's line prints. The 178th, país, country, was woven in the
# singular, país, under "countries", where its line prints "país m (plural
# países)"; it weaves países since this pass.
# quote is the clause of that line which prints the plural, its qualifiers
# kept, or "invariable" where the line says the plural is the singular. A
# page holds every word of one spelling, so the clause is this word's own
# noun's, of the seed's gender and sense. Three pages hold a second noun of
# this spelling with no such plural, and each was read by sense: sol, sun,
# is "plural soles" where sol, the note, is uncountable; mar, sea, is
# "plural mares" beside an abbreviation of marzo; and colina, hill, is
# "plural colinas" where colina, choline, is uncountable.
# tests/tools/plurals.test.ts requires every noun lex-es.tsv weaves in a
# second form to have a line here with that form, citing the noun's own
# entry, its quote printing the form, and fails on a line outliving its row.
